title: Grateful Dead Live at Portland Memorial Coliseum on 1973-06-24
lineage: set 1: SBD> ?>C> CD> EAC> SHN; set 2: SBD> MR> C> D> CD> EAC> SHN

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording with a stellar Dark Star→Eyes→China Doll sequence, though the set is incomplete and has some lyrical slips.
ai_review.review: The show shines thanks to an epic, extended Dark Star that showcases extraordinary dual‑guitar interplay and a seamless segue into a high‑energy Eyes and haunting China Doll. While the soundboard source sounds clear, the archive is missing several first‑set numbers and contains occasional vocal flubs, which keeps the overall experience from being flawless.

ai_rating.rationale: Most reviewers praise the musical performance (especially Dark Star, Eyes, and China Doll) giving high show scores, but note the recording is incomplete and has lyrical errors, lowering the technical rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Clear soundboard source; however the archive is missing several first‑set tracks (Mexicali, TLEO, etc.) and contains occasional lyrical flubs that detract from perfection.

show_quality.setlist_flow: The second‑set medley Dark Star→Eyes→China Doll is a highlight that drives the show, but the incomplete first set and some sloppy moments interrupt the overall flow.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Garcia’s guitar work is described as ‘one‑in‑a‑trillion’ with soaring solos and his vocal delivery on Dark Star receives high praise.
band_member_comments.Phil: Lesh’s bass provides a jazzy vamp that underpins the Dark Star, noted as a “percolating rhythm” and “Philo‑stop” groove.
band_member_comments.Bob: Weir contributes juicy phased effects and solid rhythm guitar; his vocal phrasing on China Doll is highlighted.
band_member_comments.Keys: Keith’s keyboards add tasteful accents near the end of the Dark Star jam, described as spilling ‘spiked coffee’ over the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann is called a “freaking genius,” laying down percolating rhythms that drive the improvisations.
